summary: Defines SNMP managed objects for controlling how alarm conditions are reported. It complements the alarm MIB by letting operators decide which alarms are reported and how.

eli5.summary: If a device has many alarms, this controls which ones ring the bell and which stay quiet.

questions: control which alarms are reported with snmp
how to suppress alarm notifications with snmp
subtitle: An SNMP MIB module that lets a manager hold back or delay alarm reports for chosen resources and alarm types.

tldr.problem: While a network resource is being provisioned, tested or maintained, it may raise alarms that nobody needs to act on. Those alarms flood technicians and managing systems with unnecessary work.
tldr.mechanism: The ARC MIB module defines a table, indexed by resource, alarm type and notification type, that puts a resource into an alarm reporting control state such as nalm, nalmTI or nalmQI. A manager creates and deletes rows to switch reporting off and back on.
tldr.outcome: Operators can run setup and testing in an alarm-free state and turn reporting on automatically or manually later. It is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted.

today: RFC 3878 is a Proposed Standard published in September 2004, and the metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated by another RFC.

sections.title: Why Control Alarm Reporting
sections.content:
The module is aimed at network operators who manage network resources. It provides a way for a manager to suppress or defer the reporting of alarm conditions, based on the resource ID and the alarm condition type.

The text gives three examples: inhibit reporting for a resource until it is problem-free, inhibit it for a specified time period, or inhibit it indefinitely until the managing system explicitly allows it again. The alarm reporting control (ARC) feature acts as an automatic in-service provisioning capability, leaving time for service setup and customer testing in an alarm-free state.

Putting a resource in ARC mode does not affect the availability of active alarm condition information for later retrieval. The design follows ITU-T Recommendation M.3100 Amendment 3, and this MIB supports a subset of its functions.
sections.eli5: When you are setting up a new toy alarm, you do not want it beeping at every test. You mute it while you work, then switch it back on.

sections.title: Place in the Management Framework
sections.content:
Managed objects live in a virtual information store called the Management Information Base (MIB), usually accessed through SNMP. Objects are defined with the Structure of Management Information, and this module is written in SMIv2 (RFC 2578, RFC 2579, RFC 2580).

The module sits at { mib-2 117 }. It reuses the ResourceId type from the Alarm MIB (RFC 3877) and the probable-cause values of the IANA-ITU-ALARM-TC module, which come from ITU-T M.3100. It adds a textual convention, IANAItuProbableCauseOrZero, that accepts any probable cause or 0.

Defining objects for storing alarms (active, history, standing, transient) and alarm notifications is out of scope.
sections.eli5: This is one more page in the big rulebook that network devices share, and it borrows the alarm names from another page instead of inventing new ones.

sections.title: The ARC Table
sections.content:
Two scalars set time intervals in seconds: arcTITimeInterval for the timed-inhibit state and arcCDTimeInterval for the count-down state. Instances of both SHOULD persist across agent restarts.

The main object is arcTable. Each row is indexed by three things:

  • arcIndex: the resource under control, for example an interface.
  • arcAlarmType: the alarm condition type. The value 0 means any probable cause applicable to the resource.
  • arcNotificationId: the notification type to suppress. The value 0.0 means all applicable notification types.

Each row also has arcState, arcNalmTimeRemaining (seconds left in the timed or count-down state, which a manager may extend or shorten), arcRowStatus and arcStorageType, which defaults to nonVolatile. If arcIndex and arcNotificationId together exceed 114 sub-IDs, column instance OIDs exceed 128 sub-IDs and cannot be accessed with SNMPv1, SNMPv2c or SNMPv3.
sections.eli5: Think of a list where each line says: this device, this kind of alarm, this kind of message, and how quiet it should be right now.

sections.title: ARC States
sections.content:
M.3100 Amendment 3 defines five states. alm: reporting is on. nalm: reporting is off. nalmTI (timed inhibit): reporting is off for a specified time interval. nalmQI (qualified inhibit): reporting is off until the entity is qualified problem-free, meaning the alarm condition is cleared. nalmQICD is a substate of nalmQI that counts down a persistence interval after the entity is problem-free.

The arcState enumeration lists only nalm (1), nalmQI (2), nalmTI (3) and nalmQICD (4). The alm state is implicit: when a resource returns to normal reporting, its row is automatically deleted, and a manager can get the same result by setting arcRowStatus to destroy.

A resource supporting ARC shall support alm and at least one of nalm, nalmTI and nalmQI. The nalmTI state returns to alm automatically when its timer expires, and nalmQI does so when the entity is problem-free, or when the count-down timer expires if nalmQICD is supported.
sections.eli5: The alarm can be fully on, fully muted, muted for a set time, or muted until things are fixed and a little waiting time has passed.

sections.title: Effect on Alarm Reports
sections.content:
The RFC states three rules for what is reported once a resource is in ARC mode:

  • An alarm raised before entering ARC mode is reported as usual, both raised and cleared.
  • An alarm raised after entering ARC mode and cleared before leaving it produces no report at all, neither raised nor cleared.
  • An alarm raised after entering ARC mode and still active when leaving it has its raised report deferred until the moment of exit. Its cleared report is sent as usual when it clears.

To create a setting, a manager sets arcRowStatus to createAndGo or createAndWait. Setting it to destroy removes the setting and resumes normal reporting. Only arcState, arcNalmTimeRemaining and arcRowStatus can be updated while a row is active.
sections.eli5: While the alarm is muted you hear nothing about quick problems that fix themselves. A problem that is still there when you unmute is announced right then.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
All six writable or creatable objects (arcTITimeInterval, arcCDTimeInterval, arcState, arcNalmTimeRemaining, arcRowStatus and arcStorageType) may be sensitive. Unprotected SET operations could disrupt operations, from omitting alarm notifications to flooding the network with unwanted ones. Suppressing or deferring an alarm can also delay diagnostic information, including information that could help identify an attack.

Reading these objects reveals settings that affect alarm generation, so GET and NOTIFY access should also be controlled. SNMP versions before SNMPv3 did not include adequate security. Implementers are RECOMMENDED to consider SNMPv3 security, including its cryptographic authentication and privacy, and deploying earlier versions is NOT RECOMMENDED.
sections.eli5: Whoever can change the mute settings could hide a real problem, so only trusted people should be allowed to touch them.
